text:
The planned Dunmarrow canal tunnel will run 11 kilometres, the North Aster Waterway Authority said Monday, confirming the figure in its latest procurement filing. The bored section would cut travel time for freight barges crossing the ridge from 4.5 hours to 55 minutes, officials said. Tender documents call for two access shafts, a maintenance spur and a water-handling system sized for 38 million cubic metres a year.

Construction is slated to start in March 2027, with first throughput targeted for late 2031. Estimated project cost is 2.8 billion lars, up from 2.4 billion last year.

For the sector, the length matters: it places Dunmarrow among the region’s largest inland works, likely tightening demand for tunnel boring rigs, marine steel and project finance.
